Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our GC reviewed the draft order form and flagged two items in the pricing exhibit that we need clarified before legal can sign off:

1) A right to surcharge in the event of material cost increases (e.g., GPU market shocks). They want explicit language and a 30-day notice plus cap at 12%/annum.
2) A clawback for credits if monthly consumption drops below committed minimums in months 3–6 (we commit to a ramp schedule). They want the math spelled out (net of usage credits).

Attached is our redline (Acme_Redline_v1.pdf) with suggested language. Can your team confirm Redwood can accept or provide counter language? We are targeting signature by Oct 28.

Appreciate a quick read.

Emily —

Appreciate the clear asks. Commercially, Acme's ramp timeline and committed units look reasonable, and we can be flexible on a modest surcharge mechanism tied to validated third-party cost indices. Proposed commercial compromises:

- Surcharge: Redwood can accept a surcharge clause capped at 10% per annum with the following controls:
  - Trigger only if our raw hardware costs (public vendor pricing index) increase by >8% quarter-over-quarter.
  - 30-day notice and the right for Acme to terminate for material adverse increases (>15% in any one quarter).

- Clawback / true-up: We can do a straight-line true-up for months 3–6 if actual usage is below committed minimums, capped at the difference between committed spend and paid usage in the quarter (no retroactive reversal of already-applied credits).

We'll share a tracked exhibit for legal review. If that broadly matches Acme's intent, Laura will draft the precise legal text.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Emily / Acme Legal —

Attached is Redwood's proposed counter-exhibit (RI-counter-exhibit-v2.pdf) with precise drafting. Highlights / rationale:

1) Surcharge language:
- We limited triggers to publicly verifiable cost indices (to avoid unilateral determination).
- Cap at 10% per annum as a compromise; language includes a quarterly reconciliation mechanism and a 30-day notice window.

2) Clawback / True-up:
- We propose a quarterly true-up calculation: (Committed Spend - Actual Paid Usage) but excluding any promotional credits and capped at 25% of the quarter's committed spend.
- No retroactive reversal of credits once invoiced; instead, future invoices will reflect the true-up. This preserves operational billing stability.

3) Governance:
- Joint escalation: if either party disputes a surcharge, there is a 15-business-day review followed by mediation before termination rights kick in.

Please review the draft and let us know line-by-line. We're open to small commercial tweaks but prefer to avoid open-ended clawback exposure.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Our GC reviewed your counter and asked for two narrow clarifications:

1) Can the surcharge cap be expressed as a rolling 12-month cap (rather than per-annum reset) to better protect against repeated quarterly bumps?
2) For the true-up cap, can we agree to an alternative of a three-month offset instead of future invoices (i.e., apply true-up against the next three monthly invoices), which helps our month-to-month forecasting.

If you accept those two items we can proceed to signature and route the order form to procurement. We are OK with mediation language.

Emily Zhang

Acme Analytics

Emily —

Thanks — we can accept both clarifications with small drafting tweaks:

- Surcharge cap: change to a rolling 12-month cumulative cap of 12% (replaces the per-annum 10% wording). This gives Acme the rolling protection you asked for while giving Redwood headroom for transient cost spikes.
- True-up payment mechanics: agree to apply the quarterly true-up across the next three monthly invoices instead of netting against indefinite future invoices. We'll add a short examples section in the exhibit for transparency.

I will update RI-counter-exhibit-v2 with those two edits and resend. Once you confirm, we can proceed to signature (happy to take the DocuSign link).
